title: Testing and Benchmarking Emerging Supercomputers via the MFC Flow Solver
problem: New supercomputers require systematic testing and evaluation; lack of portable, user-friendly benchmarking tools limits adoption validation.
motivation: CFD codes serve as valuable proxies for supercomputer evaluation; MFC provides a standardized testbed across generations of GPU and CPU architectures.
method: Multicomponent Flow Code (MFC) is a simulation tool for complex fluids, paired with an automated system that performs three tasks: compiling the code for different supercomputers, checking that results stay consistent when the code or compilers change (regression testing), and measuring how fast the code runs. By automating these steps across diverse hardware, researchers can verify whether newly built supercomputers work correctly and efficiently without setting up tests manually for each machine.
key_novelty: A portable testing framework that automatically detects compiler bugs and performance regressions (when code runs slower than it should) when running fluid-dynamics simulations on emerging supercomputers.
contributions: Automated MFC benchmarking toolchain across 50+ compute devices and 5 flagship supercomputers
Comparative evaluation across NVIDIA (5 gen), AMD (3 gen) GPUs and multiple CPU architectures
Discovery of compiler bugs and regressions on Frontier and El Capitan
limitations: CFD-specific; may not represent all application categories; compiler bug discovery is incidental.
